criterion: The home screen and the crystal layer sit on two near-black grounds under one fine static grain.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the page ground and the crystal ground are both near-black, the boundary between them is invisible, a fine monochrome grain lies over the window, and a surface further from the page reads one step lighter. No if a lighter panel appears behind the crystal, the grain animates, or the two grounds meet at a visible edge.

criterion: Reading type on every surface is a near-white neutral with secondary copy one step dimmer.
evaluation_rule: Yes if body copy reads as a near-white tone, secondary lines such as a client name read as a mid grey, and the hairlines, dividers and field borders are all faint whites laid over the ground. No if body copy is pure white, if secondary copy shares the body tone, or if a divider or field border is drawn in a colour of its own.

criterion: Beyond the crystal edges and an armed delete, one warm sand tone is the only warm colour in the studio console and on the public site.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the single warm tone appears for an invalid field, a failed save, a held field and a pinned label, and the only other colours on screen are the armed delete yellow and the two fringe tones on the crystal edges. No if a third warm or saturated hue appears on any surface.

criterion: On the public site the warm sand appears inside the privacy notice alone.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the warm tone on the reading surfaces is confined to the notice page, where it picks out the operative phrase and a link under the pointer. No if the warm tone appears on the home screen, the carousel, the grid or a case file, or on the contact surface anywhere other than a field the server rejected.

criterion: A half-transparent blue ground sits behind an unfinished chapter in the case file editor.
evaluation_rule: Yes if any ground on any surface is a translucent blue, a soft teal or any other tone from outside the product's own palette. No if every ground on every surface, the gradient behind an image chapter included, is drawn from the product's own dark neutrals.

criterion: The home screen and the studio console ship one dark mode designed through every surface.
evaluation_rule: Yes if every surface renders dark whatever the system theme preference says. No if a light theme appears under a system preference or a theme control.

criterion: Display type, reading type and the labels stand apart as three registers on every surface.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the three menu words and a case file title tower over the reading copy beside them, and the labels and the bar message sit clearly below that reading copy, so a reader places any line in one of the three registers at a glance. No if the type on a surface reads as one continuous range, or a label is set close enough to the reading copy that the two read as the same thing.

criterion: Display text carries an extralight cut and reading text a light cut.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a case file title and a grid sector render in the thinnest cut while the studio promise and case file body copy render one step heavier. No if one weight carries both, or if the register changes by colour rather than by cut and size.

criterion: Labels across the console and the public surfaces are small capitals with open letter spacing.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the console controls render as small uppercase text whose underline brightens under the pointer, the labels beside them are spaced capitals, and the three menu words on the public site stay in sentence case. No if a console control renders in sentence case, a label loses its letter spacing, a menu word arrives in capitals, or a console control rests with no underline at all.

criterion: Every public surface is flat, and the shapes that round their corners are the few the product names.
evaluation_rule: Yes if no block on the story, the carousel, the grid or a case file is boxed in a card or a panel, and the only rounded shapes are round controls, the scrollbar thumb and a device chapter frame. No if a card or a panel frames a block on any of those surfaces, or a rectangular block carries a corner radius.

criterion: A large gap on the studio story always arrives with a thin rule in a deep neutral.
evaluation_rule: Yes if each new block on the story and the contact surface opens with a wide gap carrying a one-pixel rule darker than the type. No if blocks are separated by rules of a bright tone, or if a wide gap arrives with nothing drawn across it.

criterion: A link on the notice page carries a faint underline that brightens under the pointer.
evaluation_rule: Yes if every link rests with a dim underline and draws a brighter line across itself when the pointer arrives. No if a link rests with a full-strength underline or gains one only on hover.

criterion: The scrollbar on the studio story is styled in the product's own tones.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the scrollbar track is a near-black with a translucent white thumb. No if the browser default scrollbar shows through, or the scrollbar is hidden while the surface still scrolls.

criterion: The notice page and the console share one wide centred container with labels beside the copy.
evaluation_rule: Yes if both surfaces lay labels in a narrow left column with copy or controls in a wide right column of one shared container. No if the two surfaces use different containers or stack the label above the copy at a wide window.

criterion: Every action mark is an unfilled two-unit stroke and every object mark is filled.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the close, drag and expand marks are drawn as outlines with square corners where two strokes meet, every outline at the same visible thickness, while the play, drop, arrow and menu marks are solid shapes. No if an action mark is filled, an object mark is an outline, or a stroke end or corner is rounded off.

criterion: An open layer carries a wider close control labelled for the surface behind a short white divider.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a case file closes with Close Project, the reel with Close Showreel, the grid with Close All Projects, the story with Close Story, the contact surface with Close Contact, the notice with Close Notice and the console with Close Studio, each control carrying a short vertical divider at its right edge. No if one generic close label serves every layer, a label names the wrong surface, or the divider is missing.

criterion: The interaction bar carries a message line, a thin line, a pending ring and a counter whose digits roll.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the four parts sit along the bottom centre and the counter digits roll through a clipped box when the count changes. No if the counter snaps to its new value or one of the four parts is absent.

criterion: The project grid answers the pointer with the product's own round cursor and tiles that travel.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the arrow gives way to a round drawn cursor over the grid and filtered tiles animate to their new places. No if the arrow cursor stays, or the tiles jump to their new positions in one frame.

criterion: The crystal is built from forty to sixty flat facets with a broken silhouette and a few bright faces.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the object reads as tens of flat faces, some thrown outward from the mass, with only a handful lit in any frame. No if the object reads as a smooth sphere, a wireframe, or a uniformly lit solid.

criterion: Every bright crystal edge carries a cold fringe on one side and a warm fringe on the other.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the lit edges show an opposed two-colour fringe, cyan against red. No if the edges are plain white, or the fringe reads as the same hue on both sides.

criterion: The wordmark sits inside the depth of the crystal with facets passing in front of the letters.
evaluation_rule: Yes if facets cross in front of the wordmark as the object turns. No if the wordmark floats above the whole object or sits behind all of it.

criterion: A reseed throws the crystal facets outward before the facets fall back together.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the Drop control swells the facets away from the centre and settles them into a new arrangement. No if the object cuts to its new arrangement in one frame.

criterion: The pending ring in a submit control reads as an accelerating sweep.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the ring speeds and slows through its turn. No if the ring steps around its circle at an even rate like a clock hand.

criterion: Nothing on a resting surface moves except the crystal.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a control at rest holds still and only the crystal turns while a surface sits untouched. No if a control pulses, a strip loops, or a background drifts on its own.

criterion: A layer opening over the home screen arrives by fading into place at one of three speeds.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a layer fades in and each moving thing takes one of three durations, quick under the pointer, slower near it and slower again for content. No if a layer slides in from an edge or every moment shares one duration.

criterion: The Audio control off state reuses the crossed lines of the close mark.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the sound-off mark is a speaker carrying the same crossed geometry as the close mark. No if the off state uses a struck-through circle or a different cross.

criterion: The studio story lays a narrow sector label column beside the client rows above the bottom-aligned awards.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the sector label occupies about a third of the reading column, each award renders as its name under a short white rule, and the award row in a case file footer aligns along its bottom edge. No if the label column spans the full width, an award is drawn from an image file, or the awards align along their tops.

criterion: The carousel draws its drag mark as a line with an arrowhead at each end under an almost invisible grid legend.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the drag affordance is a double-headed line and the word above the grid sectors sits at the faintest strength on the surface. No if the drag affordance is written as words or the legend reads at full strength.

criterion: A device chapter draws its frame as an unfilled rounded outline in the faintest light neutral.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the phone or tablet frame around a device chapter is an outline in a light neutral with nothing filled behind it and the screen image sitting inside. No if the frame is a filled shape, carries a drop shadow, or is drawn from a supplied picture of a device.

criterion: A showreel awaiting its film and a loading collection each render one of the four shared state layouts.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the empty reel shows the centred layout, a large heading over one shorter line with at most one control and no illustration, and a loading collection shows the skeleton layout, plain dark blocks in the shape of the list. No if the empty reel plays a placeholder film, the loading blocks shimmer or pulse, or either surface invents a fifth layout.

criterion: The notice page is set near headline size with very large gaps between the rows.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the notice copy reads at a size close to a heading with wide space between rows. No if the notice reads as small print or its rows sit at the density of an ordinary page.

criterion: The studio console reads as the same product at work: quiet, dense and organised rather than roomy.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the console rows sit closer together than the public surfaces while keeping the same type and the same restraint, so a studio member reads many case files at once. No if the console adopts a denser typeface of its own, or spaces its rows as generously as the public work.

criterion: The public site reads as an editorial object where the work is seen before any interface.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a first-time reader meets the crystal, the wordmark and the work with almost no visible interface. No if a header bar, a sidebar or a toolbar frames the public surfaces.

criterion: Each surface leads with one primary action distinct from every secondary one, and each control shows its five states.
evaluation_rule: Yes if one action on each surface is visibly the loudest and every control reads differently at rest, under the pointer, pressed, focused and unavailable. No if two actions on one surface carry equal emphasis, or a control looks the same focused as at rest.

criterion: A form field carries a thin border at rest, a thicker outlined border on focus and a warm sand border when the value is rejected.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the three field states read as three distinct borders with the rejected one carrying a warm sand message below it. No if a rejected field is marked by colour alone or the focused field is indistinguishable from the resting one.

criterion: Body text on every surface meets the AA contrast floor against its ground.
evaluation_rule: Yes if reading copy, secondary lines and labels all clear the AA ratio against the ground behind them. No if any reading text sits below that ratio.

criterion: Every corner control on the home screen answers a press inside a target of at least 44 pixels in each direction.
evaluation_rule: Yes if each corner control, form control and console control answers a press inside a target of that size. No if any control answers only inside a smaller area.

criterion: Every icon-only control carries a text label and every surface opens with one first-level heading.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a screen reader reaches a name for each corner control and finds one top-level heading per surface, visually hidden where the design shows none. No if a control announces as a bare graphic or a surface carries two first-level headings.

criterion: Reading surfaces allow a visitor to select and copy their text.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a case file body, the studio story and the notice page allow text selection. No if selection is suppressed on a reading surface.

criterion: Every state on the contact surface and in the studio console carries a second signal beyond its tone.
evaluation_rule: Yes if an unavailable control, the selected sector in the grid filter and a search match each carry a second signal beyond their tone, such as a weight, a mark or a position. No if any of those three states is told apart by colour alone.

criterion: The layout answers every width from a phone to a very wide monitor across five tiers.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the home screen, the grid, a case file and the console each recompose at phone, small tablet, laptop, desktop and very wide widths, and the dismissible card that greets a phone visitor is offered at most once. No if a surface keeps its desktop layout at phone width, or the card returns on every visit.
